events.description: A week-long competitive coding event attracting participation from all years and branches. It consists of a set of 7 problems. The participants labor relentlessly to submit efficient solutions to the problem releasing after every 24 hours.

"Math is the backbone of engineering". MathRush is a mathematical puzzle contest in which sound knowledge of mathematics together with the taste of programming will be essential to solve problems. Being a "zero, either you lead or follow.

A two-round competitive programming event designed to test participants' coding skills, problem-solving abilities, and speed. It begins with an online Codeforces contest, followed by an offline knockout round featuring one-on-one coding battles where participants compete to solve programming challenges faster and more accurately than their opponents.
rules: Round 1 (Online Qualifier): Participants will compete in an online Codeforces contest, solving algorithmic problems within a fixed time limit. This round will test their problem-solving abilities, coding efficiency, accuracy, and performance under time constraints. Top 30 participants are shortlisted.

Round 2 (Offline Knockout): Shortlisted participants will be divided in 2 groups according to their year. They will compete in one-on-one coding battles within their group, racing against their opponents to solve a given programming problem. The fastest participant to submit a correct solution will win the duel and advance.

events.description: An event aimed at simulating the software profile-based recruitment procedure for undergraduates. It consists of a series of written and coding rounds testing the technical prowess of the candidate. Interview rounds also form an integral part of the event in which the students are judged on the knowledge and confidence they exude.
Given a list of code the students are expected to dry run the code and provide output fast and accurate which will in turn be used in another set of problems

The largest puzzling event of Avishkar galvanizes even the laziest of brains into action and encourages prompt response and witty answers. Operaomnia gauges the ability of participants to play with riddles, puzzles and brain teasers

Ready to put your Agentic AI skills to the test? Develop an AI agent to tackle a given set of tasks and put it through multiple test cases. The top-performing agents will advance to a final evaluation. Build smart, experiment with your approach, and see how far your agent can go!
rules: Team eligibility: All branches (Inter-year not allowed)
Submission: Must provide GitHub repo with detailed README and demo video

events.description: Get ready to put your ML skills to the test! Participants will tackle a machine learning challenge where the goal is to build, train, and fine-tune models to achieve the best possible results. Experiment with different approaches, squeeze out every bit of accuracy, and climb the leaderboard before time runs out.
rules: Team eligibility: All branches (Inter-year not allowed)

events.description: A fun design competition where participants compete to create the worst-looking and most confusing user interface possible. Break design principles, experiment with clashing colors, and build hilariously unusable interfaces. The goal is simple: make bad design look even worse!
rules: Team eligibility: All branches (Inter-year not allowed)
Submission: Must provide GitHub repo with demo video

events.description: Get ready to dive into a code repository full of bugs, errors, and questionable coding decisions. Your mission? Hunt down those bugs and figure out how to fix them before time runs out! The person who squashes the most bugs in the shortest time takes the crown.
rules: Team eligibility: All branches (Inter-year not allowed)
Submission: Must provide GitHub repo with updated code along with a README listing every change and bug found

events.description: The Daemon is an offline and beginner friendly, Linux-based challenge where participants connect to a private server via SSH and solve increasingly difficult tasks using Linux commands and tools. It promotes hands-on learning, logical thinking, and problem-solving, with a cheat sheet provided for beginners.
rules: Team eligibility: All branches (Inter-year not allowed)

Participants will be provided with access to a Linux-based server through SSH and will be required to solve a series of challenges by exploring files, discovering hidden clues, and using Linux commands to progress through increasingly difficult levels.

events.description: A 36-hour challenge. Build an assistant that retrieves documents, queries structured databases, connects information across sources, and answers with evidence. In the final round, investigate an unseen business problem and present findings.
rules: Team Eligibility: All branches (Inter-year not allowed)

Round 1 (Implementation Round): Participants will build an AI-powered assistant capable of retrieving, querying, and connecting information from multiple data sources, including documents, reports, and structured databases, to generate accurate, evidence-backed answers.

Round 2 (Investigation Round): Teams will use their developed AI agents to investigate an unseen business problem, analyse information from different sources, and present their findings with relevant supporting evidence.
